subject: Energy
title: Offshore Drilling
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Offshore Drilling.

hook.text: About 30% of world oil comes from beneath the ocean floor—extracted from platforms and floating rigs.

buildup.text: Shallow-water platforms stand on steel legs fixed to the seabed—stable and relatively simple to operate.

discovery.text: Deepwater rigs float, held in position by thrusters—drilling in water over 1,500 meters deep.

twist.text: The North Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and offshore Brazil are major regions—each with extreme engineering challenges.

climax.text: Offshore oil costs 3–5 times more to produce than onshore—but massive reserves justify the investment.

punchline.text: Floating factories above miles of ocean—drilling into the seabed.

quiz.question: What share of world oil comes from offshore?
